pieces.file: Martin Heidegger — rich — you do not see the hammer.svg
pieces.title: You do not see the hammer
pieces.caption: A tool in use is ready-to-hand: “you don't notice the hammer, you notice the nail going in”. It becomes present-at-hand, an object staring back, “only when it breaks”. *What is real and what is a choice:* Drawing the two by fading is my way in; the page's claim is about two ways a tool can be, not about eyesight. The hammer, nail and bench are a drawing.

challenge.by: challenger · light round, batch G (ten drawn diagrams and loops) · read-only dispatch

verdicts.file: Martin Heidegger — rich — you do not see the hammer.svg
verdicts.why: The idea is right and it is the page's own move, nearly word for word ("you don't notice the hammer, you notice the nail going in"; present-at-hand "only when it breaks"), and drawing by opacity is a real idea, not words in boxes. The drawing has a fault: in the WORKING panel the hammer's handle runs down through the workbench and out the bottom, ending just above the footer text, so the hand that swings it would be under the board.

remade.file: Martin Heidegger — rich — you do not see the hammer.svg
remade.what: The working hammer's handle ran down through the bench, the broken one read as a block and a stick, and the honest line claimed more than the page. The hammer is now held above the bench with its face on the nail, the broken one lies on the bench with its handle snapped and still joined, the labels use the page's two terms, and the Merleau-Ponty avatar is dropped.
